messages:
alex: Heads up — I have a small reproducer for weird kvcache growth / page-table slot misalignment. Seen on MI250X and H100 (different flavors), not on A100. Dump below and a couple quick traces.

marta: ack, thanks. short summary of what you saw?

alex: longctx workload (64k tokens, streaming), batch=8. After ~2000 requests kvcache memory climbs linearly, and evict logic starts freeing wrong slots. Page table shows duplicate owners for the same slot id.

samir: can you paste the slab/page metadata? suspected wrap/overflow.

alex: log excerpt:
```
PAGECNT=4096
slot: 4095 owner: gpu0
slot: 0 owner: gpu1
slot: 4096 owner: gpu0  <-- this is > PAGECNT
slot: 1 owner: gpu0
EVICT: choosing slot 4096 -> accessing pagetable[0] instead
```

marta: whoa. sounds like some index arithmetic lost a modulus or an int promoted beyond 32-bit. MI250X uses 64-bit pointers in our pager; H100 uses 32-bit slot math in kernel path?

samir: quick theory: when the pager does async split-evict, we have two concurrent updates: one increments slot_index, the other writes owner. If increment doesn't wrap correctly especially across GPU-specific atomic semantics we can transiently see slot==PAGECNT before modulus. On some archs that gets written back and used.

cheng: also saw a similar pattern in trace where kernel chosen for pagewalk differed:
- H100: kernel=k_pagetable_tiled_v2 (uses atomic_mod)
- MI250X: kernel=k_pagetable_linear (uses naive add then % in host code)
If the host -> device write ordering differs, device may see raw increment > pagecnt.

alex: repro command I ran:
```
./run_infer --model lla-13b --longctx 65536 --batch 8 --gpus mi250x,mi250x --pager paged --pager-concurrency 4 --seed 42
```

marta: can you try forcing pagetable kernel to tiled_v2 on MI and see if it disappears? that isolates kernel selection.

alex: forced tiled_v2 on MI250X, still reproduce but delayed 3x. forcing linear on H100 triggers it quicker. So both kernels play a role; ordering differences across archs change exposure.

samir: posted a tiny repro script: /tmp/repro_kv_slot_shift.sh
```bash
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..5000}; do
  python perf_client.py --model lla-13b --tokens 64000 --batch 8 --pager paged || break
done
```

It reliably reproduces in ~2k iterations on MI, ~6k on H100, never on A100.

cheng: profiling snapshot (brief):
- MI250X: high stalls at kvcache_free (store-ordering), mem_barrier missing on fast-path.
- H100: high divergent branches in tiled kernel causing reorder of owner writes.

perf-bot: CI regression: perf/kvcache/growth flagged 2026-03-18 (job 1712169000) — might be related.

alex: quick hack/workaround: add atomic compare-and-swap when updating slot_index and always write modulus result back before publishing owner. Pseudocode:
```c
uint32_t old = atomic_fetch_add(&slot_idx, 1);
uint32_t wrapped = old % PAGECNT;
atomic_store(&slot_idx, wrapped);
atomic_store(&page_owner[wrapped], gpu_id);
// publish
atomic_thread_fence(seq_cst);
```
With that change memory growth stops in local runs.

marta: good. we need a proper fix and tests. action items:
1) bisect kernel selector changes between tiled_v2/linear (cheng)
2) add a deterministic unit test for slot wrap under concurrent evict (samir)
3) add telemetry for slot_index values > PAGECNT in prod (alex)
4) add safety check in pager to reject indices >= PAGECNT until fixed (marta)

samir: filing a reproducible test + small harness, will assign PR. Also adding NVLINK cross-GPU stress to reproduce cross-device races.

ops-bot: created bug ticket INF-6666 and linked perf job 1712169000.

cheng: I'll try to reproduce with different kernel compile flags (no-optimizations, memory-fence variants) and report. I suspect a subtle memory-ordering gap in our linear kernel on ROCm.

alex: thx all. I'll open PR with debug-only ASM and the CAS safety check + telemetry. If anyone else can reproduce on other HW please paste logs here.

marta: assigning samir/cheng to the fix, alex to telemetry + initial PR. will sync in tomorrow stand. :thumbsup:
